comment: The No Envy demo video (Open Agentic Web Challenge: required, under two minutes, public on YouTube). Built by the lab's shared tool: node ../codegeist/tools/video/build.mjs --plan tools/video/plan.json --raw ../work/video/raw-aw. Shots 1 and 2 are recorded by tools/video/capture.mjs; its time marks are where the captions below change. Shots 3 and 4 show the assistant and need a real model: their captions are written only after the recording exists, from what is really on screen. 'expect' and 'what' are used for the placeholder card of a trial cut (--allow-missing). Captions say what is on screen, in two lines at most.

title.heading: No Envy
title.sub: Split the rent so nobody wants to swap rooms

captions.text: An example: three housemates and three rooms that are not equal. An even split would not be fair.
Each said what every room is worth to them. The page works out who gets which room and what each pays.
Anyone can check it: in each row, the room that person got is the one they come out best on.
With an even split, two of them would want the big room.
For your own place, put in the names and the rent. No account: the numbers travel inside links.
Each housemate gets a link of their own.
Ben opens that link. Only Ben's own card can be filled in: the others' amounts did not travel with it.
The reply is another link, to send back in any message.
Opened where the sheet was started, it drops Ben's amounts in. Nothing is stored on a server of ours.

shots.what: The assistant, run by a real model: asked in plain words, it sets up a sheet with the page's own actions, finds the split and explains it. An Undo appears for what it changed.
Asked about a lease clause, it shows who it would ask (another agentic site) and waits. Nothing is contacted until the visitor allows it.

end.heading: No Envy
lines: Other agent sites can ask its agent network for a split.
Designed and built by an AI agent (Anthropic's Claude), operated by a human entrant.
